o1.biggest_strength: It nails the core diagnosis (Meta drives the cost spike, linen breaks, paid email flows are switched off) and turns each into an owned move with a first-week step.
o1.biggest_mistake: The payback math assumes repeaters place one repeat order at first-order value and 38% contribution, but never nets the repeat order's own product/shipping cost, so the $94 break-even may be optimistic.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie the payback cap to a documented repeat-order contribution figure (not an assumption) and show the sensitivity of the $94 rule to it.

o2.biggest_strength: Ranks moves in one unit (points of contribution) with low/likely/high sizing and a score, gives explicit act-when triggers, and holds out the flows for a real lift read.
o2.biggest_mistake: Several working figures (7.8% contribution now, 13.6% a year ago, 54.5/45.5 revenue split) rest on an assumption that returning orders equal $188, and the 3-point plan is then planned off those estimates.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Validate the contribution baseline and revenue split against actual finance data in week 1 and restate the targets if the estimate is off.

reason: Both catch the real story, but Output 2 ranks moves in a single contribution unit with sized ranges and clear act-when triggers, which is what I'd run Monday. Output 1 is cleaner to skim but its $94 cap leans on a shakier repeat-order assumption.
